summary: Multi-model batching causing intermittent 5xx surge and long-tail latency on dedicated runtime
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Health, Dedicated) began reporting intermittent 502/503 responses and a large increase in tail latency (~95th-99th percentile) on their chat + embedding mixed routes after we rolled out the adaptive multi-model batching policy for their tenant at ~2026-03-13T23:10:00Z. The pattern is sustained error spikes that correlate with short bursts of mixed chat+embed requests.

Impact:
- Customer observed ~15-25% request error rate (5xx) for a 30 minute window, causing degraded end-user experience in production.
- A subset of streaming sessions experienced resets.
- Affects Dedicated capacity pool for Acme Health (business-critical).

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: prod-us-east (gpu-pool-dedicated-7)
- Runtime version: inference-runtime v3.6.2+hotfix
- Scheduler: adaptive-batcher (recent rollout at 2026-03-13 23:10 UTC)
- Models in fused batching: redwood-open-chat-1 (chat), embed-mini-1 (embeddings)

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer has mixed traffic: many short chat requests (context ~80 tokens) interleaved with small embedding payloads.
2) Adaptive batching merges heterogeneous requests into single batch to improve throughput.
3) After ~10-30s of sustained mixed requests the apigw starts returning 502/503 and runtimes show worker thread stalls or exits.

Observed behavior / logs (representative):
- apigateway logs: elevated 502/503 from upstream; error spikes align with combination of many short chat + embed requests.
- runtime logs (node gpu-23): repeated "WorkerThread stalled: kv_cache_miss_loop" followed by annotation "nvml:device_reset" and runtime restart events.
- kernel logs: occasional NVML error 0xE (driver reset) at times of spike.
- metrics: gpu_util dips to 5-10% during the error window, CPU and thread contention in runtime climb; queueing latency increases before the 5xx wave.

Expected behavior:
- Adaptive batching should increase throughput without destabilizing the runtime or increasing 5xx volume. Requests should see small tail-latency increases but not runtime crashes or NVML resets.

Temporary mitigation already applied:
- Rolled back adaptive-batcher for Acme Health tenant at 2026-03-14T00:05:00Z; immediate reduction in 5xx to baseline within two minutes.
- Placed a short circuit rule at apigw to limit mixing of embed and chat routes while investigation continues.

Requester note:
Customer asked for root cause and a safe rollback path; they requested follow-up within SLA window.

investigation_notes:
Hypotheses:
1) Heterogeneous batch mixing (chat + embed) causes kv cache eviction thrash: differing KV sizes and attention cache lifetimes result in frequent reallocations and pinned locks.
2) Thread starvation: runtime worker threads block on cache locks, CPU scheduler preempts GPU progress causing driver timeouts and reset.
3) Pathological small-batch merge magnifies scheduler locks under high short-tail concurrency.
Evidence:
- Core dump shows worker blocked in kv_cache::resize path.
- NVML reset coincides with long-running CPU-side stall; GPU driver reports watchdog timeout.
Next steps:
- Add scheduler guardrail to avoid cross-model batching for dedicated tenants as immediate mitigation (in progress).
- Patch runtime to make kv_cache resize non-blocking and add backoff.
- Add telemetry: per-tenant "cross-model-batch-count" metric and kv_cache contention histograms.
- Run canary with guardrail in staging and then one dedicated customer pool before wide rollout.
resolution_notes: (Work in progress) Temporary rollback of adaptive-batching for Acme Health performed 2026-03-14T00:05Z; verified error rate returned to baseline. Planned permanent fix: scheduler guardrail + runtime non-blocking resize. Target hotfix PR created (github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4821). Postmortem to capture rollout checklist and add preflight checks for cross-model-batch safety. Customer notified of timeline and agreed to staged canary.
follow_up_actions: Create a scheduler preflight test that simulates mixed chat+embed traffic patterns and fails rollout if kv contention exceeds threshold
Implement non-blocking kv_cache resize and add unit/integration tests
Add per-tenant guardrail flag to disable cross-model batching by default for Dedicated until runtime patch is verified
Write a short runbook: how to rollback adaptive batching per tenant and how to collect core artifacts quickly
